title: Modernism in Literature
text: Modernism was a major literary movement of the early 20th century, characterized by a self-conscious break with traditional forms of writing and a desire to find new means of expression. Modernist writers rejected linear narrative, conventional plot structures, and omniscient narrators in favor of stream of consciousness, fragmented narratives, and multiple perspectives. Key modernist authors include James Joyce (Ulysses, 1922), Virginia Woolf (Mrs Dalloway, 1925), T.S. Eliot (The Waste Land, 1922), William Faulkner, and Franz Kafka. Modernism was influenced by World War I's disillusionment, Freudian psychology, and new scientific ideas about relativity and the nature of time.
